message.text: Including test files bumps the counts up—User shows up in 7 packages and Memo in 5—but my original tally excluded test files, giving User 6 packages with ~71 references and Memo 4 packages with ~51 references, so I'll rank User first, Memo second, and Attachment third. I also want to flag the distinction between different Memo store references before finalizing.

h11.

**1st: `store.User` — referenced from about 6 packages outside the data layer (~71 references); 2nd: `store.Memo` — about 4 packages (~51 references).**

The ranking, counting non-test Go files outside `store/` and excluding generated protobuf code under `proto/gen/`:

| Entity | Packages | References | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `store.User` | 6 | 71 | `server/router/api/v1` (50), `server/auth` (7), `server/notification` (6), `server/router/api/v1/test` (4), `server/router/fileserver` (2), `server/router/rss` (2) |
| `store.Memo` | 4 | 51 | `server/router/api/v1` (38), `server/notification` (11), `server/router/rss` (1), `server/runner/memopayload` (1) |
| `store.Attachment` | 3 | 37 | `server/router/api/v1` (21), `server/router/fileserver` (15), `server/router/rss` (1) |

`store.User` (`store/user.go:29`) leads because it's the currency of authentication and authorization, not just a CRUD entity: `server/auth` threads it through the authenticator and request context (`server/auth/authenticator.go`, `server/auth/context.go`), the file server resolves it to serve avatars (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`), RSS uses it for feed ownership (`server/router/rss/rss.go`), and notifications need it for recipients (`server/notification/email.go`). `store.Memo` (`store/memo.go:35`) is heavily used but concentrated in the memo-related handlers of one package.

Below the top three, `store.Inbox` and `store.MemoShare` reach 2 packages each, while `store.Reaction`, `store.MemoRelation`, and `store.UserIdentity` appear only in `server/router/api/v1`.

Three types score zero outside the data layer — `store.IdentityProvider`, `store.UserSetting`, and `store.InstanceSetting` — because callers work with the protobuf forms (`storepb.IdentityProvider`, `storepb.UserSetting`, `storepb.InstanceSetting`) instead; I verified the only matches outside `store/` are inside generated `.pb.go` files.

On method: I matched the qualified identifier `store.<Type>` with a word boundary, so `store.User` doesn't absorb `store.UserSetting`/`store.UserIdentity`, and `store.Memo` doesn't absorb `store.MemoRelation`/`store.MemoShare`. Query/mutation structs (`FindUser`, `UpdateMemo`, and so on) were excluded so the count reflects the entity types themselves. Including `_test.go` files would add `server/router/frontend` to both leaders, making it roughly 7 versus 5, which doesn't change the ordering.
